title: Predecessor shifted counting-sort invariant
statement: Let $A$ describe $n$ items, source and destination regions, key-cell addresses, a key bound $N_b$, and a counter region; let $it,kf:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and let $\mu,\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be memory maps. Assume the space bound is at most the word bound, the source, destination, and counter regions fit in memory and are pairwise disjoint, and for every $i<n$ the source contains $it(i)$, its key cell lies in memory and outside the destination and counter regions, that cell contains $kf(i)$, and $kf(i)<N_b$. If $s<N_b$ and the state in memory $\mu'$ has every item at its stable sorting position, every counter at offset $t$ with $s+1<t\le N_b$ equal to the number of keys below $t$, and every counter at offset $t<s+1$ equal to the number of keys below $t+1$, then changing the counter at offset $s+1$ to the number of keys below $s+1$ gives a state in which every item remains at its stable sorting position, counters at offsets $t>s$ through $N_b$ equal the number of keys below $t$, and counters at offsets $t<s$ equal the number of keys below $t+1$.
hypotheses_covered: The space bound is at most the word bound
Source, destination, and counter regions fit in memory
Source, destination, and counter regions are pairwise disjoint
For every item index below $n$, its source cell contains that item
Each item's key cell lies in memory and outside the destination and counter regions
Each item's key cell contains its key, which is below $N_b$
replaced:
Let $A$ describe $n$ items, their keys, the key bound $N_b$, and a counter range, and
let $[?]$ be a memory. Assume the count-sort layout conditions: memory-space is bounded
by word size; source, destination, and counter ranges lie within memory space; source
cells contain the indexed items; each item's in-bounds key cell contains its key; all
keys are below $N_b$; the source, destination, and counter ranges are pairwise disjoint;
and each key cell lies outside the destination and counter ranges. Let $s<N_b$, and
suppose all items occupy their sorted positions, each counter cell above stage $s+1$ and
at most $N_b$ contains the number of keys below its offset, and each counter cell below
$s+1$ contains the number of keys below its offset plus one. After setting the counter
cell at offset $s+1$ to the number of keys below $s+1$, the shifted-state conditions
hold at stage $s$: all items remain placed, counter cells above $s$ and at most $N_b$
contain the number of keys below their offset, and counter cells below $s$ contain the
number of keys below the next offset.
